job.title: Commercial & Property Lawyer
job.description:
Connected People is proud to be partnering with Turnbull Hill Lawyers to recruit an experienced Commercial & Property Lawyer to join their established team.

Turnbull Hill Lawyers is one of the Hunter region's most established law firms, providing legal services to individuals and businesses for more than 50 years. The firm has built an excellent reputation for providing practical, client-focused advice and enjoys strong, long-standing relationships with its clients.

The Role
This is a genuine mixed Property & Commercial Law role, offering exposure to quality, interesting and complex matters.
Your property work will include:
  • Residential and commercial property sales and acquisitions;
  • Drafting, reviewing and negotiating contracts for sale;
  • Commercial leasing matters;
  • Property transactions and settlements; and
  • Providing practical advice to individuals, investors, developers and business clients.
On the commercial side, you will work across a range of quality business and corporate matters, including more complex and high-value transactions, such as:
  • Business sales and acquisitions;
  • Complex transactions involving multi-entity businesses and structures;
  • Drafting and negotiating commercial contracts and agreements;
  • Shareholder, partnership and other business agreements;
  • Corporate and commercial advisory work; and
  • Providing ongoing commercial advice to established business clients.
You will have strong secretarial support, allowing you to focus on your legal work, client relationships and continued professional development.

About You
To be considered, you will have:
  • A minimum of 5 years PAE in property and/or commercial law;
  • A genuine interest in property and commercial law;
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills;
  • A professional, practical and client-focused approach; and
  • The ability to work collaboratively.
What's On Offer?
  • A tight-knit, cohesive and supportive team;
  • A highly established firm with a strong and consistent workflow;
  • Exposure to complex and interesting property and commercial work;
  • Strong secretarial and administrative support;
  • Exceptional training;
  • An excellent workplace culture; and
  • The opportunity to further develop your expertise across property and commercial law.
For more information or a confidential discussion about this opportunity, please contact Monica Walmsley at Connected People on 0492 300 464.

job.title: Inhouse Conveyancer / Property Lawyer / Conveyancing Paralegal
job.description:
Connected People is partnering with a large and highly regarded Newcastle-based for-purpose organisation to recruit an experienced property professional to join its collaborative in-house team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for a Conveyancer, Property Lawyer or experienced Conveyancing Paralegal looking to move in-house and work across a genuinely interesting and varied portfolio of property matters.

Rather than high-volume residential conveyancing, you’ll be involved in a broad range of interesting and often complex property transactions, including acquisitions, disposals, leases, licences, easements, covenants, subdivisions and other property dealings. 

You’ll join a fun, collaborative and supportive team environment, with the flexibility to work three days in the office and two days from home.

The Role:
Working as part of an established in-house team, you will manage and support property matters from commencement through to completion.

Depending on your level of experience, your responsibilities may include:
  • Managing property transactions including acquisitions, disposals, leases, licences, easements, covenants and subdivisions;
  • Coordinating settlements, registrations and property documentation;
  • Undertaking property and title searches and investigating land ownership and historical property interests;
  • Reviewing title issues, easements, covenants, restrictions and other land-related matters;
  • Assisting with legal and commercial due diligence;
  • Reviewing, preparing and administering property-related agreements and documentation;
  • Liaising with external solicitors, conveyancers, surveyors, valuers, planners and other specialists; and
  • Providing practical advice and support to internal stakeholders on property matters. 
There is also the opportunity to become involved in broader property governance, compliance and regulatory matters, making this a particularly interesting role for someone wanting to broaden their experience beyond traditional conveyancing. 

About You:
We are open to candidates from a range of property backgrounds. You may be a:
  • Conveyancer (Licensed or not);
  • Property Lawyer;
  • Experienced Conveyancing Paralegal; or
  • Property professional with strong experience across conveyancing, property transactions or land administration.
You will ideally have strong property and conveyancing experience, excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple matters and stakeholders.

You'll be someone who enjoys investigating more complex property issues, can work autonomously when required and equally enjoys being part of a collaborative team.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is an opportunity to take your property experience in-house and work on matters that are broader and more varied than you may typically encounter in a traditional conveyancing practice.

You’ll enjoy:
  • Hybrid working – 3 days in the office and 2 days from home;
  • A fun, supportive and collaborative team;
  • Interesting and complex property matters;
  • A large, established and highly regarded Newcastle organisation;
  • Exposure to a diverse property portfolio;
  • The opportunity to broaden your experience beyond traditional conveyancing; and
  • A role where your property expertise will contribute to an organisation with a genuine community purpose.
Apply now.

job.title: People & Culture Manager - Part-Time
job.description:
Connected People is proud to be partnering with Prelude Australia to recruit an experienced People & Culture Manager.

Prelude Australia is a not-for-profit organisation that has supported children and families for more than 40 years. Today, its highly qualified team provides best-practice early childhood and therapy supports for children from birth to twelve, including children with developmental delay and disability. Their purpose is simple but powerful: to support a positive future for all children.

The Opportunity
This is a senior, broad generalist P&C role offering approximately a 50/50 balance between strategic and operational work.

Sitting on the Executive Leadership Team, you will take genuine ownership of the people function within an organisation of approximately 37 employees. With no direct reports, this is an opportunity for someone who enjoys having autonomy, influencing at a senior level and still being hands-on when required.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Providing strategic P&C advice to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team.
  • Preparing for and leading the upcoming Enterprise Agreement bargaining process.
  • Managing ER/IR matters.
  • Leading workforce planning, organisational change and capability initiatives.
  • Strengthening Prelude Australia's approach to psychosocial risk, wellbeing and workplace compliance.
  • Coaching leaders to build their people management capability.
  • Driving proactive culture, engagement and recognition initiatives.
  • Managing HR systems, policies, processes and legislative compliance.
  • Developing strategic recruitment and long-term talent pipelines, including relationships with universities and allied health scholarship recipients.
About You
Prelude Australia is looking for someone who combines warmth, capability and proactivity.

You will be an experienced P&C leader who can confidently navigate complex people matters and advise at Executive level, while remaining approachable and connected to employees.

You will bring:
  • Previous experience as a HR Manager, People & Culture Manager or equivalent Manager-level position.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification.
  • Previous Enterprise Agreement bargaining experience desirable but not essential.
  • Strong generalist ER/IR capability.
  • Experience within a not-for-profit or closely aligned purpose-driven environment such as disability, community services, health or education.
  • The ability to operate strategically while remaining comfortable with hands-on HR delivery.
  • Strong relationship-building and influencing skills.
  • A proactive, autonomous approach and the confidence to identify what needs to be done and make it happen.
Experience in psychosocial risk, workforce planning, organisational change and strategic talent pipelines will be highly regarded.

Genuine Flexibility:
This is a rare opportunity to secure a senior P&C position at 22.8 hours per week, with opportunities to self-manage work hours flexibly across the day/fortnight, plus additional breaks to support work-life balance.

Prelude Australia is open to three full days or shorter hours across four or five days, including school-hours arrangements where workable. Ideally, hours will be spread across the week to provide greater access to P&C support.

The role will have a regular presence across Prelude Australia's Maitland, Kurri Kurri and Singleton locations, combined with some work-from-home flexibility.

What's On Offer?
  • $68.31 per hour + superannuation
  • Not-for-profit salary packaging
  • Professional development allowance
  • An additional two weeks of leave per year
  • Opportunity for an additional one week of unpaid leave in January 
  • Genuine flexibility around family and personal commitments
  • Executive Leadership Team position
  • The autonomy to shape and lead the P&C function
  • The opportunity to make a visible impact within a genuinely purpose-led organisation.
